title: Deploy probe-degradation simulation harness to tune autoscaler under partial-failure
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a reproducible simulation harness that injects controlled degradations into liveness/readiness probes and KV cache behavior across regions. The goal is to observe autoscaler decisions, circuit-breaker activations, and SLO impacts so we can tune probe thresholds, backoff windows, and autoscaler derating parameters without production risk.

Motivation:
Recent incidents showed the autoscaler oscillating when probe flaps combined with partial KV cache eviction in one region. Current probe tuning is ad-hoc; we lack a systematic way to simulate realistic degraded states (in-flight latencies, transient 5xx bursts, slow readiness transitions) and measure downstream effects (scale-up latency, throttling, routed-failover). A simulation harness will let us test candidate mitigation (graded readiness, probe dampening, regional circuit breakers) and capture deterministic metrics for rollouts.

Proposed work:
- Build a lightweight harness that can:
  - Inject latency/error patterns into probe endpoints for a subset of pods (configurable percent).
  - Simulate KV cache miss storms and forced partial eviction to mimic memory pressure.
  - Trigger synthetic client traffic shapes (spiky, sustained, warm-start) directed at specific regions.
- Measure and collect: pod readiness transitions, probe flip counts, autoscaler scaling events, queue depth, token-level latency percentiles, circuit-breaker trips, and SLO window breaches.
- Run matrix of scenarios (single-region degraded, cross-region degraded with fallback, degraded-plus-high-throughput) to evaluate:
  - Autoscaler thrash (scale-down/scale-up events per 30m)
  - Time-to-recover to baseline SLOs after degradation injection
  - Circuit-breaker effectiveness and false-positive rate
- Add experiment orchestration UI (basic) in an internal dashboard and persist results to the perf-data bucket for analysis.
- Produce recommended probe tuning: graded liveness tiers, readiness dampening, and autoscaler derating factors per region.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Harness can run repeatable scenarios against staging clusters with <10% runtime variance between runs.
2) We can reproduce the autoscaler oscillation observed in incident-IR-2026-01 and validate candidate mitigations reduce thrash by >=40% in the simulation.
3) Documented tuning recommendations with quantitative before/after metrics and a rollout plan (canary + telemetry checks).
4) At least one concrete config change (e.g., increased readiness stable window + 30s autoscaler derate) is validated in dedicated environment and ready for canary.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: implement harness primitives (probe latency inject, error bursts, KV eviction stub) and basic metrics collection.
- Week 2: run scenario matrix against dedicated staging clusters; iterate on instrumentation.
- Week 3: validate recommended config in Dedicated staging and prepare canary run in low-traffic production region.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Fake degradation may not cover all real-world failure modes; we'll prioritize reproducing past incident traces first.
- Running large scenario matrices consumes staging capacity; coordinate with Infra to reserve windows.
- Some mitigation (longer readiness windows) will increase time to scale up for real failures — trade-off between false positives and time-to-recover must be quantified per SLO.

comments: 2026-02-18 - Triage: Ravi created ticket after postmortem review of IR-2026-01. Initial scope reviewed with SRE and Runtime teams.

2026-02-22 - Design sync: Decided to target staging clusters first; focus on three degradation primitives: probe latency, transient 5xx bursts, and KV eviction. Nora volunteered to own harness implementation.

2026-02-26 - Implementation: Basic injector and metric exporter checked in (draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1429). Instrumentation emits readiness flip counter and autoscaler events to perf-data.

2026-03-03 - Early results: Reproduced autoscaler oscillation in staging using the 'probe-flap + kv-miss' scenario. Observed scale-down within 2m of transient and scale-up lag ~80s under default derate settings.

2026-03-09 - Mitigation trial: Ran candidate config (readiness-stable-window=45s, autoscaler-derate=0.6). Thrash reduced ~47% in three-run median; tail latency impact measured and within SLO for simulated traffic. Need formal analysis for multi-region fallback.

2026-03-13 - Next steps: Expand scenario matrix to include region-failure + cross-region routing; prepare dedicated canary window with Infra on 2026-03-18. Draft PR updated with opt-in feature flag for staging-only runs.
